failure_mode: Cooling fan seizure with protective thermal shutdown
symptoms: Temperature rose from about 34 C to about 73 C during discharge, THERM-201 tripped, pack went offline.
contributing_factors: Sustained discharge with fan tach at zero.
investigation_method: Telemetry review, fan tach, firmware comparison, configuration check.
evidence: Temperature trace on DEV-001; fan component CMP-0003 status Failed; threshold matched expected.
root_cause: Cooling fan bearing seizure caused a real pack temperature rise and a THERM-201 protective shutdown.
corrective_action: Replace the cooling fan and recommission.
preventive_action: Add a fan-tach alarm before temperature reaches the warning line.

symptoms: COM-214 after the 4.3.0 install, latency high, RSSI unchanged.
investigation_method: Firmware history aligned to fault time, lab latency injection, comparison with 4.3.1.
evidence: Faults begin after installed_at of 4.3.0. 4.3.1 test passes the same case.
root_cause: Firmware 4.3.0 drops healthy sessions when one-way latency exceeds 120 ms.
corrective_action: Roll back to 4.2.1 or upgrade to 4.3.1. Halt 4.3.0.
preventive_action: Require the 180 ms heartbeat test before the next communications release.

failure_mode: Commanded power blocked by a low configured limit
symptoms: Afternoon peaks flatlined near 75 kW and INV-360 repeated.
contributing_factors: Field edit without a change record.
evidence: Historical configuration row parameter_value 75 expected_value 90. Later row is 90 and 90. Peaks recovered after 18 Sep 10:00.
root_cause: Inverter Power Limit was set to 75 kW against the expected 90 kW.
preventive_action: Block field edits that do not match expected_value.

symptoms: Latency up, RSSI down, then offline.
contributing_factors: Antenna or radio hardware. Firmware was 4.2.1.
evidence: RSSI fell from about -68 dBm toward -107 dBm while latency climbed. No 4.3.0 install.
corrective_action: Replace the radio and re-aim the antenna.
preventive_action: Alert when RSSI and latency degrade together.

failure_mode: Cell-group imbalance from low busbar torque
symptoms: BAT-204 at three HW-C sites during discharge above 70 kW, with pack voltage swinging outside 740 to 770 V.
contributing_factors: Shared hardware revision HW-C and similar discharge conditions.
investigation_method: Cross-site comparison of revision, firmware, configuration, and telemetry.
evidence: Three batteries, hardware_revision HW-C, same error code, voltage instability before the fault.
root_cause: HW-C power-module busbar torque below spec.
corrective_action: Re-torque campaign and a temporary 60 kW cap.
preventive_action: Record busbar torque in the HW-C installation guide.

failure_mode: Temperature sensor drift causing false thermal warnings
symptoms: Slow temperature climb, normal voltage and current, snap-back after replacement, pack stayed online.
investigation_method: Compared the slope and the step change at replacement with the real thermal shutdown.
evidence: Reading fell by more than 12 C in one sample at the replacement time. DEV-001 did not snap back and went offline.
preventive_action: Use THERM-155 and a redundant channel before dispatching a fan crew.

symptoms: Power fell from about 78 kW to 6.5 kW in one sample and stayed down. Grid frequency stayed near 60 Hz. DC bus sagged.
investigation_method: Compared grid frequency, grid voltage, DC bus, and configuration.
evidence: Grid stayed nominal, so this is not the frequency-latch case. The power limit was already 90 kW, so this is not the 75 kW mismatch.
corrective_action: Replace the power module. Ticket is blocked on the part.

symptoms: SOC changed by about 50 points without matching energy at the step.
contributing_factors: Three unconfirmed hypotheses remain: SOC estimator bias, current-sensor offset, and standby parasitic load.
investigation_method: Compared SOC to current and power, then compared firmware and configuration with healthy peers.
evidence: Step at 2026-09-21 03:20 with current near zero. Firmware 4.2.1 matches peers. No hypothesis has confirming evidence.

symptoms: Main contactor opened during discharge. No thermal alarm.
investigation_method: Coil current measurement and comparison with the later precharge case.
evidence: Coil current was zero while the close command was present.
preventive_action: Capture coil current on every contactor-open event before ordering parts.

symptoms: Main contactor stayed open during discharge. No thermal alarm. Same outward symptom as the coil-driver incident.
investigation_method: Precharge voltage slope and coil current.
evidence: Coil current was present and DC bus voltage did not rise.
preventive_action: Do not assume the prior contactor incident's part is the cause.

failure_mode: Grid frequency excursion with latched inverter protection
symptoms: Frequency peaked at 61.28 Hz, power went to zero, frequency recovered, power stayed at zero.
contributing_factors: Utility disturbance and a latch that requires a reset.
evidence: Excursion is visible before the latch. DC bus did not sag the way the power-module failure did.
root_cause: Grid frequency excursion with a latched inverter protection trip.
corrective_action: Supervised reset. Do not replace the power module.
preventive_action: Archive the grid trace with the incident.

symptoms: Two temperature channels differ. No shutdown.
contributing_factors: Harness fretting is possible and not confirmed.
evidence: Not sufficient to pick a cause.

symptoms: INV-305 ripple above 25 V peak to peak above 40 kW.
contributing_factors: Power module capacitor aging on HW-B.
investigation_method: Ripple capture compared with a sister inverter.
evidence: Ripple exceeded spec. Sister unit showed the same mode.
root_cause: DC bus capacitor ESR rise on the inverter power module
preventive_action: Add ripple to the annual inverter inspection.
